subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics (IB convention) is:
questions.explain: Heat supplied equals the rise in internal energy plus work done by the gas.

questions.q: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its:
questions.explain: For an ideal gas, internal energy is proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: In an isothermal process on an ideal gas:
options: The change in internal energy is zero
questions.explain: With ΔU = 0, Q = W (all heat becomes work done by the gas).

questions.q: In an adiabatic process:
options: No heat is exchanged with the surroundings (Q = 0)
questions.explain: With Q = 0, ΔU = -W.

questions.q: In a constant-volume (isovolumetric) process, the work done by the gas is:
questions.explain: W = pΔV = 0, so Q = ΔU.

questions.q: Work done by a gas expanding at constant pressure is:
questions.explain: Pressure times volume change.

questions.q: A gas expands at 100 kPa by 0.020 m^3. The work done by the gas is:
The second law states that the total entropy of an isolated system:
questions.explain: Natural processes tend to increase total entropy.

questions.q: Entropy is a measure of:
questions.explain: Higher disorder means higher entropy.

questions.q: A heat engine operates by:
options: Taking in heat, doing work, and rejecting waste heat to a cold reservoir
questions.explain: Some heat must always be rejected (second law).

questions.q: An engine absorbs 1000 J and does 300 J of work. Its efficiency is:
questions.explain: Efficiency = 300/1000 = 30%.

questions.q: The maximum efficiency between two temperatures is that of a:
questions.explain: The Carnot limit depends only on reservoir temperatures.

questions.q: When heat is added and the gas also expands doing work, ΔU is:
questions.explain: ΔU = Q - W, so some heat becomes work.

questions.q: No heat engine can be 100% efficient because:
options: Some energy must be rejected as waste heat (second law)
questions.explain: A cyclic engine cannot convert all heat to work.

questions.q: On a pressure-volume diagram, work done by a gas equals:
questions.explain: Area under a p-V curve gives work done.

questions.q: In adiabatic compression, the gas temperature:
options: Rises (work done on it, no heat loss)
questions.explain: With Q = 0, work on the gas increases internal energy and temperature.

questions.q: Melting ice increases entropy because the liquid is:
questions.explain: The liquid has more accessible arrangements than the ordered lattice.

questions.q: 500 J of heat added at constant volume gives an internal energy change of:
questions.explain: W = 0 at constant volume, so ΔU = Q = 500 J.

questions.q: A refrigerator moves heat from cold to hot regions, which is allowed because it:
questions.explain: Work input keeps the process consistent with the second law.

questions.q: Over a complete thermodynamic cycle, the change in internal energy is:
questions.explain: Internal energy is a state function, so ΔU = 0 over a full cycle (Q = W).
